features.description: A faulty userspace program exits without stopping the kernel or another program.
acceptance_steps: Launch a program that deliberately faults in ring 3
Observe a nonzero exit status and no kernel panic
Launch another userspace program successfully afterward
evidence: 2026-10-30: make fault-smoke booted the guest, logged in over serial, observed USER PROCESS FAULT pid=1 vector=6 and exit status -7, then observed /HELLO output and exit status 0.

features.description: A CPU-bound user program cannot prevent the kernel shell or another runnable process from making progress.
acceptance_steps: Launch a user program that loops without syscalls or yields
Observe the shell remain responsive and run another command
Terminate the looping program and run a new userspace program successfully
evidence: 2026-10-30: make preemption-smoke launched two CPU-bound /SPIN programs; both printed SPIN_READY, kernel shell answered uptime, and both were terminated by PID.

features.description: A user can start a background program, keep using the shell, and terminate the job by PID.
acceptance_steps: Run a long-lived userspace program with &
Run another shell command while it is active
Terminate it with kill and verify later programs still run
evidence: 2026-10-30: make preemption-smoke used run /SPIN & twice, executed uptime while both were active, and killed both jobs by distinct PID.

features.description: User programs can start, wait, exit, and be reaped without hangs or resource leaks.
acceptance_steps: Launch and wait for multiple programs, including a failed program
Verify the shell remains responsive and process slots are reusable
evidence: 2026-10-30: make fault-smoke observed failed child exit -7 and healthy child exit 0; make preemption-smoke launched 70 further /HELLO children, all exited 0, exceeding the 63 non-idle slots.

features.description: Normal interaction runs in userspace, with the kernel shell available for recovery.
acceptance_steps: Boot into a userspace shell
Run, interrupt, and exit user programs without losing input or output

features.description: A user can edit a file, reboot, and reopen the same contents.
acceptance_steps: Create and edit a file through a userspace application
Reboot normally and verify exact contents
Exercise interrupted and invalid writes without corrupting unrelated files

features.description: A userspace editor can open, modify, and save text files.
acceptance_steps: Open a file, change text, save, and exit
Reopen the file after reboot and verify changes

features.description: A documented UEFI x86_64 machine can boot, accept input, access storage, and shut down.
acceptance_steps: Boot on a named physical machine from install media
Exercise input, storage, application launch, and shutdown
Record supported devices and known limitations

features.description: An application can communicate over a documented network interface and protocol.
acceptance_steps: Configure a supported network device
Send and receive application data across a network
Recover from a disconnected or malformed peer

features.description: A userspace desktop provides reliable input, windows, and application switching.
acceptance_steps: Launch and switch between two applications
Use keyboard and pointer input without freezing the desktop
Recover the desktop after an application fault
